title: Air-fryer butternut squash
subtitle: Butternut squash cubes roasted in the air fryer until caramelised.
excerpt: Cubed butternut squash tossed in oil and spices, air-fried until the edges caramelise and the inside is soft. Ready in 25 minutes. Serves four as a side.
sourceNotes: Butternut squash is an autumn and winter vegetable widely used in British cooking since the 1990s. The air fryer caramelises the cut surfaces of squash cubes more quickly than a conventional oven and without the need to manage a hot baking tray.

content.text: Butternut squash in the air fryer caramelises at the edges rather than steaming soft, which is the result you get when the cubes are too close together in the basket. Spread them in a single layer with space between. If your air fryer basket is small, cook in two batches. Cut the cubes to an even 2-3 cm so they cook at the same rate.

items.prepNote: peeled, deseeded, cut into 2-3 cm cubes (about 800 g prepared weight)

content.text: Toss the {{butternut-squash}} cubes with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt until evenly coated. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Spread in a single layer in the basket. Cook for 12 minutes, shake or toss, and cook for a further 10-13 minutes until the edges are caramelised and a skewer goes in without resistance. Taste and adjust seasoning.

items.cause: Cubes piled on top of each other.
items.fix: Cook in a single layer. If there are too many cubes to fit, cook in two batches.

items.symptom: Cubes drying out before cooking through
items.cause: Cut too small or temperature too high.
items.fix: Cut at least 2 cm per cube. Smaller pieces dry out before the heat reaches the centre.
Butternut squash skin does not cook down in the air fryer. Peel thoroughly before cutting.

content.text: Air-fryer butternut squash works as a simple side to roast chicken or pork, or as a base for a warm salad with rocket, feta, and toasted seeds. The same method and seasoning applies to sweet potato, parsnip, or carrot.
